the mechanisms that regulate the blood supply to tissues.

Ca2+, not IP3, is the intercellular communication signal in arteriole feedback vasodilation and that Ca2+ signals can be amplified by IP3Rs in endothelial cells.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the endothelium can sense the Ca2+ signal that drives vascular smooth muscle contraction and activate a feedback mechanism to suppress the vasoconstriction.
the endothelium is a Ca2+ sensor that can detect Ca2+ entry in vascular smooth muscle and initiate a feedback circuit that can suppress vasoconstriction.

The main takeaway from our work is that

Ca2+, the ubiquitous intracellular signal in cells, can pass from vascular smooth muscle cells to endothelial cells through positions aligned with the holes in the internal lamina of the arterioles to mediate feedback vasodilation that protects tissue blood.
Ca2+ signals from smooth muscle to endothelium can activate a feedback mechanism that protects tissue blood supply.
